surface-contract.purpose: Surface Contract 1 adds explicit fill layout and native multiline text state without changing Contract 0 event ordering, origin isolation, or authority.

compatibility.rule: A Contract 0 document is a valid Contract 1 document.
A hardpoint declares the minimum Surface API it requires in manifest.xml.
The base rejects a hardpoint whose declared API is newer than the renderer.

invariants.invariant: XML declares semantic structure and initial state; it contains no executable expressions.
PowerShell handlers run serially on the owning runspace, never on an Android callback.
Android callbacks update typed shadow state before enqueueing a semantic event.
Activity replacement destroys Views, not the living Surface document or its state.
Native text services remain native: IME, selection handles, and clipboard affordances are rendered by Android.

addition.target: surface stack text input button image list separator
addition.attribute: Requests the child to consume remaining space on its parent's primary axis.

state.property: Offset, SelectionStart, and SelectionEnd are UTF-16 indices. Line and Column are one-based.

surface-contract.example:
<surface id="edit" title="Edit"> <stack direction="vertical" grow="true"> <text-area id="editor" grow="true" /> <text id="cursor">Ln 1, Col 1</text> </stack> </surface>
$UI.editor.Changed = { $UI.status.Text = 'MODIFIED' } $UI.editor.CursorChanged = { param($Event) $UI.cursor.Text = "Ln $($Event.Value.Line), Col $($Event.Value.Column)" }
surface-contract.non-goals: Contract 1 does not define syntax highlighting, editor commands, menus, blades, accessibility metadata, or a general style language. Those require separate proof.
